items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: they have to hear Bill Evans

ctx.x: Okay. Well then they ought to hear the greatest jazz pianist, who is Art Tatum. I would say they have to hear Art Tatum, they have to hear Oscar Peterson of course, and they have to hear Bill Evans, and they have to hear older stuff too: James P. Johnson, Teddy Wilson, that would be enough to start with. And that’s of course in addition to what I imagine such people would already be interested in, I assume that they would know all about Chick Corea and Herbie Hancock and people more recent even than those two.…

As a jazz musician through the years, what was your take on what was happening in the real popular field. When Elvis came on the scene and all that, today’s jazz musician looks at the things, you know the rap is happening and Madonna and that kind of thing. Back then did you have an interest in that kind of music that was coming along, I mean —

items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I know there was only a brief mention of Bill Evans

ctx.x: Oh you don’t need my commentary on Ken Burns. I’ve read everything that’s floating around on the Web and various other magazine and newspaper articles. I think it’s marvelous that there is such a thing and that the publicity has been given to jazz to a degree that none of us ever would have expected. And it’s marvelous that I can stand up to a concert audience now and assume they’ve seen the show and I can say I’m going to play something which you might have heard on the Ken Burns show whenever they were talking…

much more sympathetic now than they were. Much more educated. And that’s wonderful. But the program, the series is not without its flaws and the basic flaw is that some remarkably important people were not included. And some people were mentioned and then nothing more was said of them. This is amazing. Unless I blinked I hardly saw anything about Oscar Peterson and I know there was only a brief mention of Bill Evans and Benny Carter was hardly mentioned, although I understand he was interviewed but somehow his…
